args.title: checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks – rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: After the deploy of checkout-api v2.3.1 to production, health checks failed in all regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) with an error rate of 18%. The v2.3.1-rc build was also unhealthy in staging. checkout-api was rolled back in all production regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. After the rollback, all regions run v2.3.0, the service is healthy, and the error rate is down to 0.2%. Next steps: find the root cause of the v2.3.1 failure before redeploying it, and look at why it was promoted when the staging RC was unhealthy.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all regions, and the service is healthy again.

- **Problem:** v2.3.1 was failing health checks in us-east, us-west and eu-west, with an error rate of 18%.
- **Rollback:** v2.3.0 was the most recent release that had been healthy in production. Before the rollback I confirmed it had been healthy there, so no change-manager approval was needed.
- **Check after rollback:** All three regions are on v2.3.0, the service reports healthy and the error rate is down to 0.2%.
- **Incident:** I opened SEV2 incident INC-0001 for checkout-api, which paged on-call. It describes the failure, the rollback and the result, and suggests next steps: find the root cause in v2.3.1 before redeploying it, and find out why it was released. Its test version had already failed health checks in staging before it went to production.

content.text: Most recent healthy production release is v2.3.0.
